Sample Candidate Formulas Conditioned on Earlier Tuning Results

Source: R/formula_sampling_adaptive.R
sample_candidate_formulas_adaptive.Rd

The second stage of a two-stage formula search. Stage one is [sample_candidate_formulas()] scored by a tuning run; this function learns from that run and draws new formulas: 1. the best models are kept (`top_quantile` of the rows by `metric`); 2. the number of terms of those models gives the size range of the new formulas (the 25th percentile to the median of the winners' sizes); 3. terms that appear more often among the winners are drawn more often (their share among the winners, plus a small floor so that no term is shut out); 4. optionally, terms whose effect points the wrong way are dropped (see `effects`).

Usage

sample_candidate_formulas_adaptive(
  prior_results_df,
  metric = "IBS",
  lower_is_better = TRUE,
  top_quantile = 0.25,
  filter_direction = TRUE,
  effects = NULL,
  effect_scale = c("ratio", "coef"),
  n_formulas = 5L,
  formula_col = "formula",
  response = NULL,
  required = character(),
  seed = NULL,
  env = parent.frame(),
  data = NULL
)

Arguments

prior_results_df

A data frame of earlier results with a formula column (text or formula objects) and a `metric` column, such as the output of [as_tuning_results()].

metric

Name of the performance column (default `"IBS"`).

lower_is_better

`TRUE` (default; IBS, Brier, AIC) or `FALSE` (concordance, AUC).

top_quantile

Share of rows kept as winners, between 0 and 1 (default 0.25).

filter_direction

If `TRUE` (default) and `effects` is given, terms with an unfavourable effect are dropped from the pool. Without `effects` there is nothing to filter on and this is ignored.

effects

Optional data frame with columns `term` and `estimate`: the univariate effect of each term (for example from [cox_single()] or [glm_single()]).

effect_scale

`"ratio"` (default; hazard or odds ratios, favourable when above 1) or `"coef"` (coefficients, favourable when above 0).

n_formulas

Number of distinct formulas wanted.

formula_col

Name of the formula column (default `"formula"`).

response

Left-hand side as text; by default the one of the first formula.

required

Terms that are in every formula.

seed

Optional integer; see [sample_candidate_formulas()].

env

Environment of the formulas.

data

Optional data frame (training rows): winning terms that are zero-variance columns of it are dropped from the pool unless `required`; see [sample_candidate_formulas()].

Value

The tibble of [sample_candidate_formulas()]; the pool, size range and weights used are in the attribute `"adaptive"`.

Details

Term and size choices come from the rows given, so pass results from the **training** folds only if the new formulas are to be assessed on held-out data (see the data-boundary note of [sample_candidate_formulas()]).

See also

[sample_candidate_formulas()], [as_tuning_results()]

Examples

prior <- data.frame(
  formula = c("y ~ a + b", "y ~ a + c", "y ~ a + b + c", "y ~ d", "y ~ d + e", "y ~ e"),
  IBS = c(0.10, 0.11, 0.12, 0.20, 0.22, 0.25)
)
sample_candidate_formulas_adaptive(prior, top_quantile = 0.5, n_formulas = 3, seed = 1)
#> # A tibble: 3 × 4
#>      id formula   terms     n_terms
#>   <int> <list>    <list>      <int>
#> 1     1 <formula> <chr [2]>       2
#> 2     2 <formula> <chr [2]>       2
#> 3     3 <formula> <chr [2]>       2
